Citation/Source: Texas Education Agency – Geospatial Engineering and Land Surveying Program of Study
Key Finding: Texas CTE program of study for geospatial engineering and land surveying; regional approval required based on labor market data for high-wage high-skill careers.
Gap/Limitation: No published evaluation of student outcomes or workforce entry rates; limited to regions with labor market justification.

Citation/Source: Klein ISD – Geospatial Engineering & Land Surveying Pathway (Klein Collins HS)
Key Finding: First-of-its-kind Texas high school pathway allowing students to earn AS in GIS plus industry certs (AutoCAD; NSPS CST I; FAA drone pilot) with dual credit through Lone Star College. Industry partnership with Gratia Geomatics/S&V Surveying.
Gap/Limitation: Single-district case study; no published data on graduation rates; diversity demographics of enrolled students not publicly reported.

Citation/Source: Gratia Geomatics – Klein ISD Program Feature
Key Finding: Surveying firm donates weekly instruction time to Klein Collins students; program founder Isidro Garza (RPLS) helped design curriculum through CTE Advisory Council.
Gap/Limitation: Relies on volunteer industry professionals; scalability and replicability not assessed.

Citation/Source: Southern California Surveyors Joint Apprenticeship Committee (SC Survey JAC)
Key Finding: Three-year apprenticeship combining field training with classroom instruction; Chainman and Chief of Party tracks; explicitly recruits veterans with GI Bill benefits.
Gap/Limitation: No published completion rates or demographic data; limited to Southern California region.

Citation/Source: Technical Engineers Apprenticeship (TEA) – Surveyor Program
Key Finding: California-based surveyor apprenticeship combining hands-on field training with classroom learning; employer-sponsored graduated wage scale.
Gap/Limitation: No published outcome data or diversity metrics.

Citation/Source: Bolton & Menk – Registered Apprenticeship Programs
Key Finding: Two-year apprenticeship for Survey Technician or Construction Project Representative; active in Iowa and North Carolina with planned expansion.
Gap/Limitation: Newly established; no longitudinal outcome data yet; limited geographic scope.

Citation/Source: New Jersey Society of Professional Land Surveyors – Apprenticeship Program
Key Finding: Offers mentorship and curriculum-based apprenticeship pathway for aspiring surveyors in New Jersey.
Gap/Limitation: Minimal public information on structure; enrollment or completion data not available.

Citation/Source: Apprenticeship.gov – Surveying Occupations Listings
Key Finding: Federal registry of registered apprenticeship opportunities for Surveyors (17-1022.00) and Surveying/Mapping Technicians (17-3031.00) nationwide.
Gap/Limitation: Aggregated listings only; no analysis of program quality or outcomes.

Citation/Source: Cleveland State Community College – Surveying Concentration AAS
Key Finding: 63-credit AAS in Engineering Systems Technology with Surveying Concentration designed for immediate workforce entry.
Gap/Limitation: No published placement rates or demographic data on graduates.

Citation/Source: St. Cloud Technical and Community College – Land Surveying/Civil Engineering
Key Finding: AAS program with transfer pathway to St. Cloud State University for BS in Land Surveying & Mapping Science.
Gap/Limitation: Transfer and completion rates not publicly reported.

Citation/Source: Kansas City Kansas Community College – Surveying Technology
Key Finding: Program prepares graduates for Kansas licensing exam through Kansas State Board of Technical Professions; covers photogrammetry GPS and GIS.
Gap/Limitation: No published pass rates for licensing exam or employment outcomes.

Citation/Source: Wake Tech Community College – Geomatics Technology
Key Finding: Geomatics Technology program with transfer pathway to NC A&T for BS in Geomatics; graduates employed as field technicians or office support.
Gap/Limitation: No diversity data or retention statistics published.

Citation/Source: Cape Fear Community College – Land Surveying (Geomatics)
Key Finding: Program blending surveying cartography and GIS; prepares students for geomatics careers.
Gap/Limitation: Limited published outcome or demographic data.

Citation/Source: Tidewater Community College – Land Surveying Certificate
Key Finding: 27-credit certificate; graduates with 6 years experience eligible for Fundamentals of Surveying Exam and State Land Surveyor-in-Training designation.
Gap/Limitation: Long experience requirement (6 years) limits rapid workforce entry; no published enrollment trends.

Citation/Source: North Carolina A&T State University – BS in Geomatics
Key Finding: Only HBCU with ABET-accredited 4-year geomatics program; ranked No. 3 nationally for online GIS degrees (2020); 80-90% placement within 6 months at ~$70K starting salary; received NCEES Surveying Education Award 3rd place in 2021 and 2022.
Gap/Limitation: Only one HBCU identified nationally with this program; no published data on racial demographics of graduates or pipeline from HBCUs to surveying licensure.

Citation/Source: PMC – Career Transition Experiences of Military Veterans (qualitative study)
Key Finding: Qualitative study (n=15) identified 4 themes in veteran career transition: necessity of preparation; impacting factors; loss of structure; and establishing civilian identity.
Gap/Limitation: Small sample; not specific to surveying or geospatial careers; general transition challenges only.

Citation/Source: Southern California Surveyors JAC – Veterans Apprenticeship
Key Finding: SC Survey JAC explicitly recruits veterans and supports GI Bill benefits for surveying apprenticeship training.
Gap/Limitation: No published data on veteran enrollment numbers; completion rates or outcomes not reported.

Citation/Source: DOD SkillBridge Program
Key Finding: Allows active-duty service members civilian work experience during last 180 days of service; could connect to surveying firms but no surveying-specific SkillBridge programs identified.
Gap/Limitation: No evidence of surveying-specific SkillBridge partnerships; significant gap in connecting military surveyors (12T) to civilian surveying careers.

Citation/Source: MOS 12T Technical Engineer Specialist – Career Profile
Key Finding: Military role closely aligned with civilian surveying; training includes CAD GPS geodetic surveys and topographic mapping over 17-week AIT at Fort Leonard Wood.
Gap/Limitation: No formal military-to-civilian surveying transition pipeline documented; no data on how many 12T soldiers enter civilian surveying careers.

Citation/Source: GoArmy.com – 12T Technical Engineer Career Page
Key Finding: Official Army career page for 12T; skills include GPS technology geodetic/construction surveys CAD systems and topographic mapping.
Gap/Limitation: No mention of civilian licensure pathways or transition support specific to professional land surveying.

Citation/Source: ASCE – Diversity Equity and Inclusion
Key Finding: ASCE MOSAIC committee leads DEI efforts; hosted first Justice Equity Diversity and Inclusion Engineering Workforce Summit; participated in Engineering Workforce Consortium Workshop.
Gap/Limitation: Broad civil engineering focus; no surveying-specific diversity data or programs identified.

Citation/Source: Hatch S. – Diversity by Design: Guide to Fostering Diversity in Civil Engineering Workforce (ASCE Press)
Key Finding: Early ASCE publication on fostering diversity in civil engineering workforce.
Gap/Limitation: Over 20 years old; predates current demographic shifts and DEI frameworks; no surveying-specific content.

Citation/Source: ASCE/NGA – Strategies to Address Engineering Workforce Challenges
Key Finding: National Governors Association convening identified actionable workforce strategies; SIU Carbondale example of free 10-week training for disadvantaged communities with guaranteed DOT employment.
Gap/Limitation: Focus on civil engineering broadly; surveying not specifically addressed.

Citation/Source: Civil Engineering Degree Apprenticeship Pathway (CEDAP) – Contra Costa County
Key Finding: $5M federal grant for structured community college to civil engineering career pathway targeting women low-income and underrepresented minorities.
Gap/Limitation: New program; no outcome data yet; focused on civil/transportation engineering not surveying specifically.

Citation/Source: ICERES/NABTU – Diversity Equity and Inclusion Initiatives in the Construction Trades
Key Finding: Union apprenticeship programs show greater gender and racial diversity than non-union programs; women completion rates higher in union programs (37.6% vs 23.4%).
Gap/Limitation: Construction trades broadly; no surveying-specific breakout data; does not address professional/licensed surveying.

Citation/Source: Economic Policy Institute – Measuring Diversity in Construction Apprenticeship Programs
Key Finding: Data show higher rates of women Hispanic workers and workers of color in union-based apprenticeships than nonunion programs.
Gap/Limitation: No surveying-specific data; aggregated across all construction trades.

Citation/Source: NABTU – Workforce Development Programs Increasing Diversity
Key Finding: Pre-apprenticeship programs and community-based organization partnerships identified as effective strategies for diverse recruitment into building trades.
Gap/Limitation: Not specific to surveying; no evaluation metrics for individual programs published.

Citation/Source: UMSL – Geospatial Workforce Development Pilot Program
Key Finding: $5M federal DOD funding to launch geospatial workforce development pilot at UMSL in partnership with NGA and T-REX; K-12 through higher ed pipeline; part of GeoFutures initiative near Next NGA West campus.
Gap/Limitation: Brand new program (Feb 2026); no outcome data; focused on geospatial intelligence not traditional land surveying.

Citation/Source: National Geospatial Innovation Hub Advancement Act (S.5024 / FY25 NDAA)
Key Finding: Federal legislation establishing 5-year geospatial workforce pilot program near NGA facilities; requires annual reports to Congress through FY2030.
Gap/Limitation: Intelligence/defense focus; may not directly benefit civilian land surveying workforce; outcome reporting not yet available.

Citation/Source: NSPS Foundation – Surveying Scholarships
Key Finding: Over $97K in scholarships annually through NSPSF; NSPS and state societies distribute approximately $350K/year total. Includes Trig-Star ($7500) Board of Directors ($2000) and named memorial scholarships.
Gap/Limitation: Scholarship amounts relatively modest; limited to students already enrolled in surveying programs; does not address pipeline into programs or diversity recruitment.

Citation/Source: Trig-Star Program – NSPS
Key Finding: National mathematics competition for high school students using trigonometry in surveying context; winners eligible for scholarships.
Gap/Limitation: Awareness/recruitment tool but no published data on whether participants actually enter surveying careers.

Citation/Source: Be A Surveyor – Scholarship Resources
Key Finding: Aggregated scholarship listing for surveying students from NSPS and state societies.
Gap/Limitation: Resource portal only; no data on scholarship impact on workforce pipeline.
